newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firmer despite new U.S. barrels.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firmer despite new U.S. barrels.

text.p: NWE gas oil was firmer on Monday as a tight physical market helped to push benchmark IPE futures $4 higher, traders said.
With demand for both diesel and heating oil strong, traders shrugged off the prospect of 300,000-400,000 tonnes of U.S. product hitting the European market in October.

Just one day before new EU low sulphur diesel rules come into force, the market for 0.05 percent material looked bullish, with premiums talking at around $18/$20 a tonne cif NWE over IPE October futures.
Diesel barges were bid at Oct IPE +$15 and offered at +$17.
Demand for heating oil in the key German market was strong, with inland dealers reporting heavy end-user restocking.
Heating oil barges were discussed at Oct IPE +$7.50/$8.50, while on the cargo market, a German refiner was bidding for DIN at Nov IPE +$7 cif Hamburg.
At least three prompt Russian handy-sized cargoes were on offer, with differentials talked around Nov IPE +$5/$7 cif NWE.
Further out in the month, bids for Russian cargoes were seen at quotes m/m -$6.50 fob Ventspils.
IPE Oct and Nov contracts both closed $4 up at $232.50 and $223.25 respectively. --Rosalind Russell, London +44 171 542 5387
